correctness.rationale: For any real 2x2 SPD matrix with unequal eigenvalues, one-node Lanczos is exactly the Rayleigh logarithm. Diagonalization gives the exact trigonometric Rayleigh factorization recorded in RESULT.md. The absolutely uniformly convergent log Fourier expansion proves the bias and dilogarithm variances by Parseval. A simple identity for perpendicular Rayleigh products gives the transformed the symmetric arcsine beta law law. Countermonotone rearrangement, proved via strict exchange inequalities and quantile approximation, makes perpendicular pairing the variance/MSE minimum for every arbitrary coupling of the fixed Haar marginals, with the claimed equality condition. The hyperbolic-tangent parameterization and Taylor series give the small-contrast coefficients. The standalone package verifier passed 252 exact-rational product tests, 870 finite-grid rearrangement tests, 35 CDF checks, 21 quadrature comparisons and six asymptotic constant checks; these are supplemental, not infinite proofs.

originality.rationale: The inspected primary 2022 randomized matrix-free quadrature work uses iid sampled weighted spectral measures; the closely related 2021 work establishes spectral approximation bounds. The later BOLT paper exploits orthonormal block probes but changes the statistic and can be exact when its block spans all of the full two-dimensional space, unlike the specified scalar one-node estimator. Searches for aliases, arcsine laws, dilogarithm, antithetic/countermonotone optimal coupling and stronger results found no inspected implication of the combined exact law; residual unindexed-specialist priority risk remains.
residual_risks: An equivalent specialized derivation of the logarithmic Rayleigh pair law could exist in unindexed or inaccessible literature; searches cannot establish independent priority.

value.rationale: The nontrivial natural invariant is exact finite-sample MSE of a widely used scalar one-node quadrature primitive with exactly two directions. Optimizing direction dependence has direct mathematical motivation: randomized trace estimators often couple or orthogonalize probes. The theorem proves that iid sampling suffers leading order quadratic error in the logarithmic spectral gap while optimal antithetic probes achieve quartic error near equal eigenvalues, with a nonzero Jensen/quadrature bias that coupling cannot remove. The distributional beta law quantifies tails, not merely a small empirical gain. Its scope is restricted to this scalar architecture; a full 2x2 block method can be exact and is not claimed inferior.
